proposals.before: In the fourth year Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the turmoil, he pardoned all except robbers who injured their victims, deserters from military service, and officials who had perverted justice.
proposals.after: In the fourth year Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the turmoil, he pardoned theft that was not robbery injuring the owner, deserters from military service, and officials who had perverted the law.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盜非劫傷其主及征人逃亡、官吏枉法，皆原之 lists categories that were pardoned (皆原之), matching the literal; the idiomatic inverted this into an exceptive reading without support from 惟/不原.

proposals.before: Afterward he again ordered the Vice Director Pei Ji and fifteen others to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.
proposals.after: Afterward he again ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and a group of fifteen in all to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.
proposals.reason: Chinese 僕射裴寂等十五人 means Pei Ji and others totaling fifteen persons, not Pei Ji plus fifteen additional people; the idiomatic correctly has fourteen others.

proposals.before: How can one commit the lightest punishment and yet sometimes die?"
proposals.after: How can one incur the lightest punishment and yet sometimes die?"
proposals.reason: 犯至輕之刑 means to incur or suffer the lightest punishment, not to "commit" the punishment itself.

proposals.before: Capital prisoners were reported monthly to the Ministry of Justice, and censors conducted inspections.
proposals.after: Capital prisoners were reported monthly by the Ministry of Justice, and censors conducted inspections.
proposals.reason: 刑部月一奏 means the Ministry of Justice submitted a monthly report, not that reports were sent to it.

proposals.before: Officials of fifth rank and above rode to the place of execution under supervision of the Court of Judicial Review, or were granted death at home.
proposals.after: Officials of fifth rank and above rode to the place of execution under supervision of the Director of the Court of Judicial Review, or were granted death at home.
proposals.reason: 大理正 is the Director of the Court of Judicial Review; the idiomatic rendering drops that specific office.

proposals.before: After Zhang Jungu's death, however, judges treated lenient misjudgment as the cautionary lesson, while harsh misjudgment went unpunished—and from that point the law grew gradually stricter.
proposals.after: After Zhang Yungu's death, however, judges treated lenient misjudgment as the cautionary lesson, while harsh misjudgment went unpunished—and from that point the law grew gradually stricter.
proposals.reason: 張蘊古 is the same Zhang Yungu named earlier; Jungu is a mistransliteration of 蘊古.

proposals.before: Yet from the death of Zhang Jungu onward, judicial officials took erroneous leniency as a warning; when there was erroneous severity, no penalty was imposed—from this the clerical law gradually tightened.
proposals.after: Yet from the death of Zhang Yungu onward, judicial officials took erroneous leniency as a warning; when there was erroneous severity, no penalty was imposed—from this the clerical law gradually tightened.
proposals.reason: 張蘊古 matches earlier Zhang Yungu; Jungu is the same transliteration error in the literal English.

proposals.before: In Kaiyuan 3, Yellow Gate Commissioner Lu Huai-shen and others compiled the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.
proposals.after: In Kaiyuan 3 under Xuanzong, Yellow Gate Commissioner Lu Huaishen and others compiled the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 玄宗 present in the Chinese and literal, and hyphenates Lu Huaishen unnaturally.

proposals.before: Under Emperor Xuanzong, Left Guard Command warehouse clerk Zhang Cui arranged the penal code by category, appended administrative edicts, and compiled the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; the Ministry of Justice was ordered to promulgate it.
proposals.after: Under Emperor Xuānzong, Left Guard Command warehouse clerk Zhang Kui arranged the penal code by category, appended administrative edicts, and compiled the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; the Ministry of Justice was ordered to promulgate it.
proposals.reason: 宣宗 is Xuānzong, easily confused with 玄宗 Xuánzong already in this chunk; 戣 is Kui, not Cui.

proposals.before: In Emperor Xuanzong's time, Warehouse Clerk of the Left Guard Command Zhang Cui classified the penal code into categories, appended administrative edicts, and produced the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to promulgate it.
proposals.after: In Emperor Xuānzong's time, Warehouse Clerk of the Left Guard Command Zhang Kui classified the penal code into categories, appended administrative edicts, and produced the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to promulgate it.
proposals.reason: Same 宣宗/玄宗 ambiguity and 戣 misread as Cui in the literal English.

proposals.before: After Xu Jingye, Prince of Yue Zhen, Prince of Langye Chong, and others raised armies against her, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.
proposals.after: After Xu Jingye, Zhen the Prince of Yue, Chong the Prince of Langye, and others raised armies against her, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.
proposals.reason: English fuses the princely titles with personal names as 'Yue Zhen' and 'Langye Chong'; Chinese 越王貞 and 琅邪王沖 are Zhen, Prince of Yue, and Chong, Prince of Langye.

proposals.before: Interrogators treat harsh severity as merit, inventing charges from nothing to outdo one another, each boasting of the other's cruelty.
proposals.after: Interrogators treat harsh severity as merit, inventing charges from nothing to outdo one another, each vaunting cruelty.
proposals.reason: Chinese 相矜以虐 means they mutually boast of cruelty, not specifically of each other's cruelty.

proposals.before: The notorious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and killed several thousand people. After he was captured, an amnesty was proclaimed. Daizong was inclined to spare his life, but the chief ministers argued he should be dismembered and salted. The emperor did not consent, yet in the end Gao Yu was beaten to death.
proposals.after: The notorious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and ate several thousand people. After he was captured, an amnesty was proclaimed. Daizong was inclined to spare his life, but the chief ministers argued he should be dismembered and salted. The emperor did not consent, yet in the end Gao Yu was beaten to death.
proposals.reason: Chinese 啗人數千 denotes cannibalistic devouring; idiomatic 'killed' understates the source verb shared with the literal 'devoured'.

proposals.before: Considering their wholehearted devotion and compassion for all beneath Heaven, they may truly be called benevolent!
proposals.after: Considering their wholehearted devotion and compassion for others, they may truly be called benevolent!
proposals.reason: Chinese 推心惻物 has no reference to Heaven; the idiomatic rendering invents 'all beneath Heaven'.

proposals.before: Minister of Works Yu Di also urged the emperor to use harsh punishments to recover sovereign authority. The emperor told the chancellors, "Di harbors treacherous designs and wants me to lose the people's hearts."
proposals.after: Minister of Works Yu Di also urged the emperor to use punishments to recover sovereign authority. The emperor told the chancellors, "Di harbors treacherous designs and wants me to lose the people's hearts."
proposals.reason: Chinese 用刑 does not specify harshness; the intensifier is an idiomatic invention.

decisions.reason: 皆原之 pardons the listed classes: 盜非劫傷其主, 征人逃亡, and 官吏枉法. The before text wrongly turns them into exceptions; the proposed after matches the Chinese and the literal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 盜非劫傷其主及征人逃亡、官吏枉法，皆原之

decisions.after: Afterward he again ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and others, fifteen persons in all, to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.
decisions.reason: 僕射裴寂等十五人 is a total of fifteen including Pei Ji, so “fifteen others” is wrong; the proposed “a group of fifteen in all” is still awkward English, so restate the inclusive count clearly.
犯至輕之刑 is to incur or undergo the lightest punishment; “commit the … punishment” misreads 犯 with 刑 as the object.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安得犯至輕之刑而或致死

decisions.reason: 刑部月一奏 makes the Ministry of Justice the agent that memorializes monthly about capital prisoners, not the recipient of reports.
大理正 names the Director of the Court of Judicial Review as supervisor; omitting 正 understates the office.
張蘊古 is Zhang Yungu, as earlier in the chapter; Jungu is a bad reading of 蘊古.
The same 張蘊古 requires Zhang Yungu in the literal field; Jungu is the parallel transliteration error.
玄宗開元三年 requires naming Xuanzong, and 盧懷慎 is Lu Huaishen without a hyphenated given name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 玄宗開元三年，黃門監盧懷慎

decisions.reason: 宣宗 is Xuānzong, distinct from 玄宗, and 張戣 is Zhang Kui; Cui and undiacriticized Xuanzong alone conflate persons and misread the given name.
The literal has the same 宣宗/張戣 errors; Xuānzong and Zhang Kui restore the Chinese names.
越王貞 and 琅邪王沖 are Zhen, Prince of Yue, and Chong, Prince of Langye; “Prince of Yue Zhen” fuses title and personal name.
相矜以虐 means they mutually boast by means of cruelty, not that each boasts of the other’s cruelty.

decisions.after: The notorious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and devoured several thousand people. After he was captured, an amnesty was proclaimed. Daizong was inclined to spare his life, but the chief ministers argued he should be dismembered and salted. The emperor did not consent, yet in the end Gao Yu was beaten to death.
decisions.reason: 啗人數千 is cannibalistic devouring, so “killed” is too weak; “ate” is semantically right but less natural than “devoured,” which matches the source verb and the existing literal.
推心惻物 has compassion for creatures/others only; “all beneath Heaven” is invented.
用刑 means use punishments; the Chinese does not add 重/酷, so “harsh” is an unsupported intensifier.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0008 removes the hyphenated English personal name that came only from the bad idiomatic spelling of 盧懷慎.
Accepted r0009 restores the diacritic that distinguishes 宣宗 from 玄宗 in English while keeping zh and pinyin.
Accepted r0009 shows English Zhang Cui came only from misreading 戣; the personal-name claim must read Zhang Kui.
The given-name claim’s English Cui is the same misreading of 戣; revise to Kui with unchanged pinyin.
Accepted r0011 shows the fused English title came from the bad translation of 越王貞; the name claim should separate personal name and princely title.
Accepted r0011 likewise requires unfusing 琅邪王沖 in the title-name claim.
Revised r0013 shows the event action “killed-thousands” came from understating 啗; replace with devouring while keeping claim identity and evidence.
